questions.nlq: Could you tell me which delivery drivers have exceeded the average number of deliveries for their respective routes in 2018, including their employee names, truck licence numbers, the percentage of delivered versus other status deliveries they've handled, and whether their delivery performance is above the overall company average?

meanings.gt_sql:
WITH Yearly_Deliveries AS (
    SELECT 
        od.driver_employee_id,
        dlr.route_id,
        od.truck_id,
        od.delivery_status_code,
        od.delivery_date
    FROM Order_Deliveries od
    JOIN Delivery_Route_Locations dlr ON od.location_code = dlr.location_code
    WHERE strftime('%Y', od.delivery_date) = '2018'
),
Route_Driver_Truck_Counts AS (
    SELECT 
        route_id,
        driver_employee_id,
        truck_id,
        COUNT(*) AS delivery_count,
        SUM(CASE WHEN delivery_status_code = 'Delivered' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS delivered_count
    FROM Yearly_Deliveries
    GROUP BY route_id, driver_employee_id, truck_id
),
Route_Averages AS (
    SELECT 
        route_id,
        AVG(delivery_count) AS avg_deliveries_for_route
    FROM Route_Driver_Truck_Counts
    GROUP BY route_id
),
Company_Average AS (
    SELECT AVG(delivered_count * 100.0 / delivery_count) AS overall_avg_delivery_rate
    FROM Route_Driver_Truck_Counts
)
SELECT 
    e.employee_name,
    t.truck_licence_number,
    ROUND(rdtc.delivered_count * 100.0 / rdtc.delivery_count, 2) AS delivery_percentage,
    CASE WHEN rdtc.delivered_count * 100.0 / rdtc.delivery_count > (SELECT overall_avg_delivery_rate FROM Company_Average) THEN 'Yes' ELSE 'No' END AS above_company_avg
FROM Route_Driver_Truck_Counts rdtc
JOIN Route_Averages ra ON rdtc.route_id = ra.route_id
JOIN Employees e ON rdtc.driver_employee_id = e.employee_id
JOIN Trucks t ON rdtc.truck_id = t.truck_id
WHERE rdtc.delivery_count > ra.avg_deliveries_for_route;

questions.nlq: : Could you tell me for each customer who has placed at least one successful order, the total amount they have spent on successful orders, the average number of days between the order date and the delivery date for those orders, and the percentage of their orders that were delivered on time (where on‑time means the delivery occurred within three days of the order date)?

meanings.gt_sql:
WITH order_delivery AS (
    SELECT actual_order_id, MIN(delivery_date) AS delivery_date
    FROM Order_Deliveries
    GROUP BY actual_order_id
),
successful_orders AS (
    SELECT c.customer_id,
           ao.actual_order_id,
           ao.actual_order_date,
           od.delivery_date,
           SUM(p.product_price) AS order_total
    FROM Customers c
    JOIN Regular_Orders ro ON c.customer_id = ro.distributer_id
    JOIN Actual_Orders ao ON ro.regular_order_id = ao.regular_order_id
    JOIN order_delivery od ON ao.actual_order_id = od.actual_order_id
    JOIN Actual_Order_Products aop ON ao.actual_order_id = aop.actual_order_id
    JOIN Products p ON aop.product_id = p.product_id
    WHERE ao.order_status_code = 'Success'
    GROUP BY c.customer_id, ao.actual_order_id, ao.actual_order_date, od.delivery_date
)
SELECT
    SUM(order_total) AS total_amount_spent,
    AVG(julianday(delivery_date) - julianday(actual_order_date)) AS avg_days_between_order_delivery,
    100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN julianday(delivery_date) - julianday(actual_order_date) <= 3 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*) AS pct_orders_delivered_on_time
FROM successful_orders
GROUP BY customer_id
HAVING COUNT(*) >= 1;
